text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has appointed former cabinet member and director of the Government Office Le Xuan Trinh as chairman of a newly established management board for industrial and processing zones throughout the country.

-- The anti-corruption draft ordinance is expected to be open for public discussions shortly. The legislation, drafted last month at the request of Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, provides a definition of corruption and suggests that offenders in cases involving more than 300 milion dong ($26,894) should be sentenced to death or life imprisonment.

-- One captain and two senior lieutenants of the Border Guard Command were arrested last week for alleged involvement in the largest international drug trafficking organisation ever exposed in Vietnam.
-- Vietnam's estimated growth rate was 9.34 percent last year, the second consecutive year in which growth has passed nine percent.
-- Communist Party General Secretary Do Muoi has called on SOS International to build more villages for orphans in mountainous and central areas of Vietnam.
-- State-run PetroVietnam expectes crude oil output of nine million tonnes in 1997.
-- Three people were killed and one injured by a mine explosion in the northern coastal town of of Halong on December 31.
-- Saigon Port handled 7.3 million tonnes of cargo in 1996, up 22 percent from 1995.
-- Vietnam exported 2.97 million tonnes of rice in 1996, up 48.59 percent from last year.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet called for more competent state apparatus in the coming years.
-- Vietnam's population had swelled to 77 million by the end of 1996, making the country Southeast Asia's second most populous.
